messages:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGED: High-generation-latency-usc-west — paging oncall; severity P1. Link: https://pager.example/INC12345. Symptoms: 95th pct token latency spike for short prompts (<=64 tokens) in hosted API. Possible kernel/quantization regression.
Alex Chen: I'm on it. Seen a big jump in 95p started ~14:02 PDT. Rolling back last runtime patch would be my first retry if safe.
Maria Gomez: confirming customer impact: initial logs show increased tail latency for ~0.8% of requests, mostly small prompt uses (chat and quick-gen routes). Could affect interactive UIs.
Jordan SRE: I can take the rollback if we have signoff. Need to know what models/pools impacted — I see load concentrated on g4dn-dedicated-3 in us-west-2.
Ellie Ops: Notifying statuspage draft owners. I'll start a short initial update for status.redwood.ai once we confirm impact classification.
Alex Chen: Quick triage: kernel change deployed at 13:59 PDT to speed up kv-cache, but new quantized path seems to increase per-token latency for short sequences on certain GPUs. Repro locally with the patch.
Maria Gomez: For customer-facing copy, we should avoid blaming the patch. Draft initial: ```We are investigating increased response times for text generation in US-West. Some users may see slower responses for short prompts. Our engineering team is actively working on a fix and will provide updates every 30 minutes.```
Ryan (Product): +1 to that copy. Also include guidance: recommend retry/backoff for clients and link to status/subscribe.
Jordan SRE: Rollback plan: revert runtime patch to previous kernel image (image v2026-11-08). Estimated safe window: 2–3 minutes to push and verify per AZ. Will run canary then bulk.
Ellie Ops: Checklist before publish: 1) Confirm impacted capacity & region 2) Confirm SLA-impact yes/no 3) Post initial note 4) Start periodic updates 5) Escalate to legal if data loss risk. We have 1 and 2 in progress.
Maria Gomez: SLA impact: looks like transient latency spike, no errors/5xx, not an SLA breach per current thresholds but could push some requests over customer latency SLOs. Mark as "customer-impact: degraded-performance" in status page.
Alex Chen: I'm going to trigger rollback canary now on podset us-west-2a. Will watch p95 and p99 for 5 minutes.
Oncall Bot: action logged: rollback-canary started by Alex Chen (run id: run-84721).
Jordan SRE: Canary shows p95 returning to baseline in us-west-2a after revert. Rolling to us-west-2b/c now.
Ellie Ops: Draft initial status page (please review):
```
Incident update - Engineering currently investigating increased text-generation latency in US-West (us-west-2). Some customers may experience slower responses for short prompts (<=64 tokens). We have identified a recent runtime patch as the likely cause and are performing a rollback. We will post updates every 30 minutes. No data loss or 5xx errors observed at this time.
```
Maria Gomez: Legal quick-check: is the phrasing ok around "no data loss"? Legal (triage), can you confirm?
Legal (triage): Good to state "no evidence of data loss" rather than absolute "no data loss". Suggest small wording tweak.
Ellie Ops: Updated copy with legal note: ```... No evidence of data loss or data integrity issues has been observed.``` Ready to publish initial.
Ryan (Product): Also add "Affected systems: hosted API generation endpoints in US-West" and "Workaround: clients may add a short retry/backoff; streaming clients may see delayed first tokens."
Ellie Ops: Publishing now. Statuspage initial update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-11-08-latency-spike.
Oncall Bot: statuspage_posted by Ellie Ops (post id sp-3321).
Alex Chen: Rollback complete across region at 14:18 PDT. Metrics: p95 back to baseline, p99 trending down. Continuing monitoring.
Jordan SRE: Starting 30-minute cadence updates. Next update at 14:48 PDT.
Maria Gomez: Periodic update (14:48 PDT): ```Engineering completed rollback of a runtime kernel change that caused increased tail latency for short prompts. Systems are recovering; we continue to monitor. No evidence of data loss.```.
Ellie Ops: Posting update to status page now. Update posted.
Ryan (Product): Incoming customer asks: please prepare suggested customer note we can paste into support responses. Draft: ```We experienced a temporary increase in response latency for text-generation requests in US-West. The issue was caused by a recent runtime change and has been rolled back. If you continue to see elevated latency, please contact support and include request IDs. We apologize for the disruption.```
Maria Gomez: I'll publish that to triage doc for support agents.
Oncall Bot: monitoring alert cleared for generation-latency-usc-west at 15:02 PDT.
Alex Chen: Final health check looks good for 20 minutes. I'm marking the incident resolved on my end.
Ellie Ops: Preparing resolved notice for status page. Proposed resolved copy:
```
Resolved - Engineering has reverted the runtime change and performance has returned to normal for text-generation endpoints in US-West. No evidence of data loss. If you are still experiencing issues, please reach out to support and include request ids. The incident start time: 13:59 PDT. Resolved: 15:02 PDT.
```
Jordan SRE: Go ahead and publish resolved. I've archived run-84721 and attached logs to the incident runbook.
Ellie Ops: Published resolved notice. Close checklist: 1) Postmortem owner assigned 2) Follow-up evals scheduled 3) Customer notification template sent to account teams.
Alex Chen: I'll own postmortem, will include root cause, timeline, remediation, and a regression test to catch similar kernel regressions in CI. ETA for initial draft: EOD tomorrow.
Ryan (Product): Thanks all. Good cadence and quick rollback. :thumbsup:
Oncall Bot: Incident INC12345 marked RESOLVED by Ellie Ops at 15:02 PDT. Incident thread closed per oncall rules.
